reason: The hero's code layer. Drawn by CSS `content` so it is not in the accessibility tree, and WCAG 1.4.3 exempts incidental text that is part of a picture with other significant visual content. Measured at 1.46:1 under the headline and 2.71:1 to the right; raising it to 4.5:1 would make the background a foreground. The lede and the spec column carry their own paper so no real content is ever read against it.

LINE Login's own button, emitted by the LINE plugin inside WooCommerce's login form. LINE's brand guidelines fix it at #06C755 with white text, which is 2.26:1 - the official asset fails WCAG 1.4.3 as designed. Recolouring a third party's sign-in control breaks the recognition it exists for; the fix belongs to LINE, not to this page. The page's own primary button was corrected to ink-on-accent (5.73:1) in the same pass.

WordPress's visually-hidden pattern: a 1px clipped box that keeps the text in the accessibility tree while hiding it from sight. Being clipped is the whole mechanism, not a defect - the audit is right that 11px of text sits in a 1px box, and that is exactly what a screen reader needs it to do.
